terminology_correction.firewall: The word jet is used here as an observable morphology/route metaphor. It is not a claim of an astrophysical relativistic jet, directed-energy beam, or artificial emitter.

kamil_physical_morphology.impactor: single iron mass or tight fragment cluster, Gebel Kamil Ni-rich ataxite
observable_components: atmospheric luminous bolide trail before ground impact
downrange plume of shrapnel and melt spherules predicted for oblique impact
radial bright ejecta rays on the ground
dark and white impact glass plus Fe-Ni droplets/spherules
kamil_physical_morphology.important_boundary: No eyewitness description of the Kamil event is currently identified; the visual sequence is reconstructed from impact physics, not from a surviving Kamil-specific narrative.

reference_chain: Kitchen, Ramesside Inscriptions I, KRI I 27:3-4
Epigraphic Survey, Reliefs and Inscriptions at Karnak IV, plate/text discussion
Comelli et al. 2016 note that a Karnak text of this period probably describes a meteorite
karnak_text_gate.short_translation_excerpt: like a shooting star, scattering its fire in flames when it emits its tail
karnak_text_gate.why: The passage compares the king to a shooting star; it does not provide a date, Kamil place-name, crater description, or explicit statement that a contemporary impact was witnessed.
karnak_text_gate.candidate_identification_note: This is a strong candidate for the Karnak meteor-like text cited by later meteoritics literature, but the dead ISMA-CNR database footnote prevents proving that this exact passage is the sole text intended by Comelli et al.

chronology_overlap.interpretation: Sety I falls near the early edge of the favored 1-sigma Kamil interval and within the favored 2-sigma interval. This is chronology compatibility only, not event identity.

ancient_iron_sky_language.period: comes into use as a composite term in the 19th Dynasty / 13th century BCE
ancient_iron_sky_language.relation_to_kamil: chronologically compatible cultural context for awareness that iron could come from the sky
ancient_iron_sky_language.firewall: The concept of celestial iron and meteoritic iron use in Egypt predates any secure Kamil dating; therefore Kamil cannot be assumed to have created the concept.

glass_geochemistry_update.meaning: Kamil impact glass is not a simple frozen sample of bulk meteorite composition; strong metal-silicate fractionation occurred. Therefore anomalous Au/Pt/Ir tests must use phase-resolved measurements rather than a naive bulk mixing line.
glass_geochemistry_update.important_gap: The cited Kamil glass table provides Fe-Ni-Co baseline values but does not itself close the Au/Pt/Ir inclusion question. Direct Au/Pt/Ir measurements on individual metal-rich glass blebs remain a valid next material gate.

bulk_meteorite_noble_metal_baseline.use: natural meteoritic baseline against which any alleged gold-rich inclusion must be tested

reverse_pass.question: If an ancient text really described a Kamil-like event, what observables should appear without using the word meteorite?

reverse_pass.result: The Karnak Sety I simile independently contains shooting-star + fire/flame + tail morphology.

reverse_pass.control: These are generic meteor/royal-power images and can exist without a local impact. Text alone cannot localize Kamil.
Kamil geology independently requires a real iron hypervelocity impact with an oblique downrange plume; therefore the SKY_FIRE observable does not require an exotic jet mechanism.

reverse_pass.survivor: A Kamil-like bolide would plausibly have looked like a directed column/trail of fire to an observer, and a near-contemporary Karnak text uses exactly this class of imagery.

next_gate.name: KAMIL_FIRE_COLUMN_TEXT_AND_BLEB_FORENSICS_V2
tasks: Obtain a facsimile/transliteration of the relevant Sety I Karnak line and compare all manuscript/edition readings of the shooting-star/fire/tail terms.
Search New Kingdom and Late Bronze Age Egyptian texts for the combined token set STAR/HEAVEN + FIRE/FLAME + FALL/DESCEND + WEST/SOUTHWEST/DESERT, without Kamil-name priming.
Search for geographic toponyms and expedition routes that could independently localize a phenomenon toward the far southwestern desert.
Retrieve phase-resolved Kamil glass/bleb chemical data and specifically test Au-Pt-Ir-Ni-Co on individual metallic inclusions rather than bulk glass.
Compare Kamil against Wabar, Henbury and other iron-impact controls to determine whether the same fire-column textual morphology and metal-in-glass signatures are generic.
next_gate.promotion_rule: Promote beyond observable analogy only if an independently dated/localized text and a non-generic material signature converge without post-hoc tuning.
